title: Geometry, Triangles & Trigonometry
sub: 20 FRQs + 25 MCQs • Difficulty Progression • Cross-Lesson Synthesis

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: Two parallel lines $\ell_1 \parallel \ell_2$ are intersected by a transversal $t$. If a pair of consecutive interior (co-interior) angles have measures $(3x + 15)^{\circ}$ and $(2x - 5)^{\circ}$, find $x$ and the measure of both angles.
questions.answer: Consecutive interior angles are supplementary: $(3x + 15) + (2x - 5) = 180 \Rightarrow 5x + 10 = 180 \Rightarrow 5x = 170 \Rightarrow x = 34$. The two angles measure $3(34) + 15 = 117^{\circ}$ and $2(34) - 5 = 63^{\circ}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, the exterior angle at vertex $C$ measures $134^{\circ}$, and the interior angle $\angle A$ measures $58^{\circ}$. Find $\angle B$ and $\angle ACB$.
questions.answer: By the Exterior Angle Theorem, $\angle A + \angle B = 134^{\circ} \Rightarrow 58^{\circ} + \angle B = 134^{\circ} \Rightarrow \angle B = 76^{\circ}$. The interior angle at $C$ is $\angle ACB = 180^{\circ} - 134^{\circ} = 46^{\circ}$.

questions.q: In right triangle $ABC$ shown below, $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$, $AC = 15$, and $BC = 8$. Find (a) the hypotenuse $AB$, (b) $\sin A$, (c) $\cos A$, and (d) $\tan B$.
questions.answer: (a) By the Pythagorean theorem, $AB = \sqrt{15^2 + 8^2} = \sqrt{289} = 17$. (b) $\sin A = \dfrac{8}{17}$. (c) $\cos A = \dfrac{15}{17}$. (d) $\tan B = \dfrac{15}{8}$.

questions.q: Find the exact perimeter and area of an equilateral triangle whose altitude has length $6\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{cm}$.
questions.answer: In a $30^{\circ}\mathrm{-}60^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ half-triangle, altitude $h = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s = 6\sqrt{3} \Rightarrow s = 12\,\mathrm{cm}$. Thus the perimeter is $3s = 36\,\mathrm{cm}$ and the area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(12)(6\sqrt{3}) = 36\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{cm^2}$.

questions.q: A square has diagonal of length $10\sqrt{2}\,\mathrm{m}$. Find its side length, perimeter, and area.
questions.answer: In a $45^{\circ}\mathrm{-}45^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ right triangle, $d = s\sqrt{2} = 10\sqrt{2} \Rightarrow s = 10\,\mathrm{m}$. Perimeter $= 4s = 40\,\mathrm{m}$, and Area $= s^2 = 100\,\mathrm{m^2}$.

questions.q: Two sides of a triangle have lengths $7$ and $12$. State the strict inequality for all possible lengths $x$ of the third side, and find how many integer values $x$ can take.
questions.answer: By the Triangle Inequality Theorem, $|12 - 7| < x < 12 + 7 \Rightarrow 5 < x < 19$. The possible integer lengths are $6, 7, \dots, 18$, which gives $18 - 6 + 1 = 13$ integer values.

questions.q: In $\triangle PQR$, $PQ = PR$ (isosceles) and the vertex angle $\angle P$ measures $44^{\circ}$. Find the measure of each base angle $\angle Q$ and $\angle R$.
questions.answer: By the Isosceles Triangle Theorem, $\angle Q = \angle R = \dfrac{180^{\circ} - 44^{\circ}}{2} = \dfrac{136^{\circ}}{2} = 68^{\circ}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Intermediate Modeling (8–14)

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, segment $DE$ is parallel to base $BC$ with $D$ on $AB$ and $E$ on $AC$. Given $AD = 6$, $DB = 9$, and $DE = 8$, find the length of $BC$ and the ratio of the area of $\triangle ADE$ to the area of $\triangle ABC$.
questions.answer: Since $DE \parallel BC$, $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$ with scale factor $k = \dfrac{AD}{AB} = \dfrac{6}{6 + 9} = \dfrac{6}{15} = \dfrac{2}{5}$. Thus $\dfrac{8}{BC} = \dfrac{2}{5} \Rightarrow BC = 20$. The area ratio is $k^2 = \left(\dfrac{2}{5}\right)^2 = \dfrac{4}{25}$.

questions.q: In right triangle $DEF$ with $\angle F = 90^{\circ}$, $\sin D = \dfrac{5}{13}$. Find $\cos E$, $\cos D$, and $\tan E$.
questions.answer: Since $D$ and $E$ are complementary ($D + E = 90^{\circ}$), $\cos E = \sin D = \dfrac{5}{13}$. By the Pythagorean identity, $\cos D = \sqrt{1 - (5/13)^2} = \dfrac{12}{13}$, and $\tan E = \cot D = \dfrac{12}{5}$.

questions.target: Geometric Mean Theorems in Right Triangles
questions.q: In right triangle $ABC$, the altitude $CD$ is drawn to the hypotenuse $AB$. If $AD = 4$ and $DB = 9$, find the length of the altitude $CD$ and both legs $AC$ and $BC$.
questions.answer: By the Geometric Mean (Right-Triangle Altitude) Theorem: $CD = \sqrt{AD \cdot DB} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 9} = 6$. Since $AB = 4 + 9 = 13$, $AC = \sqrt{AD \cdot AB} = \sqrt{4 \cdot 13} = 2\sqrt{13}$ and $BC = \sqrt{DB \cdot AB} = \sqrt{9 \cdot 13} = 3\sqrt{13}$.

questions.target: Interior & Exterior Angles of Regular Polygons
questions.q: Find the measure of one interior angle and one exterior angle of a regular $15$-sided polygon (pentadecagon).
questions.answer: Each exterior angle of a regular $n$-gon measures $\dfrac{360^{\circ}}{n} = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{15} = 24^{\circ}$. Therefore each interior angle measures $180^{\circ} - 24^{\circ} = 156^{\circ}$.

questions.q: A surveyor stands $40\,\mathrm{m}$ from the base of a vertical radio tower on level ground. The angle of elevation to the top of the tower is $60^{\circ}$, and the surveyor's eye level is $1.6\,\mathrm{m}$ above the ground. Find the exact height of the tower and its decimal approximation to two decimal places.
questions.answer: Height above eye level $= 40\tan 60^{\circ} = 40\sqrt{3}\,\mathrm{m}$. Adding eye height gives $H = 40\sqrt{3} + 1.6 \approx 69.28 + 1.6 = 70.88\,\mathrm{m}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, the angle bisector of $\angle A$ meets side $BC$ at point $D$. If $AB = 10$, $AC = 15$, and $BC = 20$, find the exact lengths of $BD$ and $DC$.
questions.answer: By the Angle Bisector Theorem, $\dfrac{BD}{DC} = \dfrac{AB}{AC} = \dfrac{10}{15} = \dfrac{2}{3}$. Since $BD + DC = 20$, we have $BD = \dfrac{2}{5}(20) = 8$ and $DC = \dfrac{3}{5}(20) = 12$.

questions.q: An isosceles trapezoid has parallel bases of lengths $10\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $26\,\mathrm{cm}$ and non-parallel legs of length $17\,\mathrm{cm}$. Find the height $h$, the area, and the length of each diagonal of the trapezoid.
questions.answer: Dropping altitudes from the shorter base splits the longer base into $8 + 10 + 8$. By the Pythagorean theorem, $h = \sqrt{17^2 - 8^2} = 15\,\mathrm{cm}$. Area $= \dfrac{10 + 26}{2} \times 15 = 270\,\mathrm{cm^2}$. Each diagonal is the hypotenuse of a right triangle with legs $10 + 8 = 18$ and $15$: $d = \sqrt{18^2 + 15^2} = \sqrt{549} = 3\sqrt{61}\,\mathrm{cm}$.

sections.heading: Part I — Free-Response Questions (FRQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, the vertices are $A(1, 2)$, $B(9, 2)$, and $C(5, 8)$. Verify that $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles, find the length of the altitude from $C$ to $AB$, and determine the coordinates of the centroid $G$.
questions.answer: Base $AB$ is horizontal of length $9 - 1 = 8$. Side $AC = \sqrt{(5-1)^2 + (8-2)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{52} = 2\sqrt{13}$ and $BC = \sqrt{(5-9)^2 + (8-2)^2} = 2\sqrt{13}$, so $AC = BC$. The altitude from $C(5, 8)$ to $y = 2$ has length $8 - 2 = 6$. The centroid is $G = \left(\dfrac{1+9+5}{3}, \dfrac{2+2+8}{3}\right) = (5, 4)$.

questions.q: In a right triangle, one leg is $7\,\mathrm{cm}$ longer than the other leg, and the hypotenuse is $17\,\mathrm{cm}$. Set up and solve a quadratic equation to find the lengths of the two legs and the sine of the smaller acute angle.
questions.answer: Let the shorter leg be $x$ and the longer leg be $x + 7$: $x^2 + (x + 7)^2 = 17^2 \Rightarrow 2x^2 + 14x + 49 = 289 \Rightarrow x^2 + 7x - 120 = 0 \Rightarrow (x + 15)(x - 8) = 0$. Since $x > 0$, the legs are $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $15\,\mathrm{cm}$, and the sine of the smaller acute angle (opposite the $8\,\mathrm{cm}$ leg) is $\dfrac{8}{17}$.

questions.target: Law of Cosines & Trigonometric Triangle Area
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB = 7$, $BC = 8$, and $\angle B = 60^{\circ}$. Use the Law of Cosines to find the exact length of side $AC$ and the exact area of $\triangle ABC$.
questions.answer: By the Law of Cosines, $AC^2 = 7^2 + 8^2 - 2(7)(8)\cos 60^{\circ} = 49 + 64 - 56 = 57 \Rightarrow AC = \sqrt{57}$. The area is $\dfrac{1}{2}(7)(8)\sin 60^{\circ} = 28 \cdot \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2} = 14\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: Triangle $ABC$ is inscribed in a circle of diameter $AB = 20\,\mathrm{cm}$. If $\cos A = \dfrac{3}{5}$, find the lengths of chords $AC$ and $BC$ and the area of the region inside the circle but outside $\triangle ABC$.
questions.answer: By Thales' Theorem, $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$ because $AB$ is a diameter. Thus $AC = AB\cos A = 20\left(\dfrac{3}{5}\right) = 12\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $BC = \sqrt{20^2 - 12^2} = 16\,\mathrm{cm}$. Triangle area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(12)(16) = 96\,\mathrm{cm^2}$; circle area $= \pi(10^2) = 100\pi\,\mathrm{cm^2}$. Region area $= (100\pi - 96)\,\mathrm{cm^2}$.

questions.target: Inscribed Square via Similar Right Triangles
questions.q: A square is inscribed inside a right triangle with legs $6$ and $12$ so that one vertex of the square coincides with the right-angle vertex of the triangle and the opposite vertex lies on the hypotenuse. Find the side length $s$ of the square.
questions.answer: Let the square have side $s$. The upper-right small right triangle has legs $6 - s$ and $s$, and is similar to the $6\mathrm{-}12$ right triangle: $\dfrac{6 - s}{s} = \dfrac{6}{12} = \dfrac{1}{2} \Rightarrow 12 - 2s = s \Rightarrow 3s = 12 \Rightarrow s = 4$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, medians $AD$ and $BE$ are perpendicular to each other and have lengths $AD = 9$ and $BE = 12$. Using the centroid ratio $2 : 1$, find the length of side $AB$ and the area of $\triangle ABC$.
questions.answer: The centroid $G$ divides each median in a $2 : 1$ ratio, so $AG = 6, GD = 3$ and $BG = 8, GE = 4$. Since $AD \perp BE$ at $G$, in right triangle $AGB$ we have $AB = \sqrt{6^2 + 8^2} = 10$. The area of orthogonal-diagonal quadrilateral $ABDE$ (or using $\triangle ABC = 3 \cdot \triangle AGB$): $[AGB] = \dfrac{1}{2}(6)(8) = 24$, and since the three sub-triangles $AGB, BGC, CGA$ have equal area, $[ABC] = 3(24) = 72$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Foundational Concepts (21–28)

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 42^{\circ}$ and $\angle B = 73^{\circ}$. What is the measure of $\angle C$?
questions.answer: The interior angles of a triangle sum to $180^{\circ}$: $\angle C = 180^{\circ} - (42^{\circ} + 73^{\circ}) = 65^{\circ}$.

questions.q: In a right triangle, the legs have lengths $9$ and $12$. What is the length of the hypotenuse?
questions.answer: By the Pythagorean theorem (a $3\mathrm{-}4\mathrm{-}5$ multiple scaled by $3$), $c = \sqrt{9^2 + 12^2} = \sqrt{225} = 15$.

questions.q: If $\sin(3x - 10)^{\circ} = \cos(2x + 25)^{\circ}$, where both angles are acute, what is the value of $x$?
questions.answer: By the cofunction identity, the two acute angles are complementary: $(3x - 10) + (2x + 25) = 90 \Rightarrow 5x + 15 = 90 \Rightarrow 5x = 75 \Rightarrow x = 15$.

questions.q: What is the sum of the interior angles of a convex octagon ($8$ sides)?
questions.answer: Sum of interior angles $= (n - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = (8 - 2) \times 180^{\circ} = 1080^{\circ}$.

questions.q: Triangles $ABC$ and $DEF$ are similar, with $AB$ corresponding to $DE$. If $AB = 6$, $BC = 10$, and $DE = 9$, what is the length of $EF$?
questions.answer: Set up the proportion $\dfrac{EF}{BC} = \dfrac{DE}{AB} \Rightarrow \dfrac{EF}{10} = \dfrac{9}{6} = 1.5 \Rightarrow EF = 15$.

questions.q: In a $30^{\circ}\mathrm{-}60^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ right triangle, the side opposite the $30^{\circ}$ angle has length $7$. What is the length of the side opposite the $60^{\circ}$ angle?
questions.answer: In a $30^{\circ}\mathrm{-}60^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ triangle, the legs are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3}$, so the side opposite $60^{\circ}$ is $7\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: In the figure below, lines $\ell$ and $m$ are parallel. If $\angle 1 = 128^{\circ}$, what is the measure of its alternate interior angle’s supplement?
questions.answer: The alternate interior angle also measures $128^{\circ}$, so its supplement measures $180^{\circ} - 128^{\circ} = 52^{\circ}$.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of side lengths CANNOT form a triangle?
questions.answer: In $5, 9, 14$, the sum of the two shorter sides is $5 + 9 = 14$, which fails the strict triangle inequality $a + b > c$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Exam Practice (29–37)

questions.q: In right triangle $PQR$ shown below, $\angle R = 90^{\circ}$, $PR = 12$, and $\tan P = \dfrac{3}{4}$. What is the perimeter of $\triangle PQR$?
questions.answer: Since $\tan P = \dfrac{QR}{PR} = \dfrac{3}{4}$ and $PR = 12$, we get $QR = 9$. Then $PQ = \sqrt{12^2 + 9^2} = 15$, so the perimeter is $12 + 9 + 15 = 36$.

questions.q: Two similar triangles have perimeters in the ratio $3 : 7$. If the area of the smaller triangle is $27\,\mathrm{cm^2}$, what is the area of the larger triangle?
questions.answer: Area scales as the square of the linear (perimeter) ratio: $\dfrac{A_2}{27} = \left(\dfrac{7}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{49}{9} \Rightarrow A_2 = 3 \times 49 = 147\,\mathrm{cm^2}$.

questions.q: In an isosceles triangle with two sides of length $13$ and base of length $10$, what is the area of the triangle?
questions.answer: The altitude to the base bisects the base into segments of length $5$, forming two $5\mathrm{-}12\mathrm{-}13$ right triangles with height $h = 12$. Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}(10)(12) = 60$.

questions.target: Finding Number of Sides from Interior Angle
questions.q: If each interior angle of a regular polygon measures $165^{\circ}$, how many sides does the polygon have?
questions.answer: Each exterior angle measures $180^{\circ} - 165^{\circ} = 15^{\circ}$. Since exterior angles sum to $360^{\circ}$, $n = \dfrac{360^{\circ}}{15^{\circ}} = 24$ sides.

questions.target: Geometric Mean Theorem for Right-Triangle Legs
questions.q: In right triangle $ABC$ with $\angle C = 90^{\circ}$, altitude $CD$ is drawn to hypotenuse $AB$. If $AC = 10$ and $AD = 5$, what is the length of $AB$?
questions.answer: By the Right-Triangle Leg Geometric Mean Theorem, $AC^2 = AD \cdot AB \Rightarrow 10^2 = 5 \cdot AB \Rightarrow AB = 20$.

questions.q: A $25$-foot ladder leans against a vertical wall with its base $7$ feet from the wall. If the top of the ladder slides down the wall by $4$ feet, how many feet does the base of the ladder slide away from the wall?
questions.answer: Initially, the top is at height $\sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = 24\,\mathrm{ft}$. After sliding down $4\,\mathrm{ft}$ to height $20\,\mathrm{ft}$, the new base distance is $\sqrt{25^2 - 20^2} = 15\,\mathrm{ft}$. Thus the base slides out by $15 - 7 = 8\,\mathrm{ft}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $D$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $E$ is the midpoint of $AC$. If the area of trapezoid $DBCE$ is $45$, what is the area of $\triangle ABC$?
questions.answer: Midsegment $DE$ forms $\triangle ADE \sim \triangle ABC$ with ratio $1 : 2$, so $[ADE] = \dfrac{1}{4}[ABC]$ and trapezoid $[DBCE] = \dfrac{3}{4}[ABC] = 45 \Rightarrow [ABC] = 60$.

questions.q: If $\theta$ is an acute angle such that $\sin\theta = 3\cos\theta$, what is the value of $\sin\theta\cos\theta$?
questions.answer: Since $\tan\theta = 3$, a right triangle has opposite leg $3$, adjacent leg $1$, and hypotenuse $\sqrt{10}$. Thus $\sin\theta\cos\theta = \left(\dfrac{3}{\sqrt{10}}\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{10}}\right) = \dfrac{3}{10}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A = 30^{\circ}$, $\angle C = 45^{\circ}$, and $AB = 12$. What is the exact length of $BC$?
questions.answer: Drop altitude $BD$ to $AC$: in the $30^{\circ}\mathrm{-}60^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ triangle $ABD$, $BD = \dfrac{1}{2}(12) = 6$. In the $45^{\circ}\mathrm{-}45^{\circ}\mathrm{-}90^{\circ}$ triangle $CBD$, $BC = BD\sqrt{2} = 6\sqrt{2}$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging & Cross-Lesson Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: What is the radius of the circle inscribed in a right triangle with legs $9$ and $40$?
questions.answer: The hypotenuse is $\sqrt{9^2 + 40^2} = \sqrt{81 + 1600} = 41$. The inradius of a right triangle is $r = \dfrac{a + b - c}{2} = \dfrac{9 + 40 - 41}{2} = 4$.

questions.target: Slope as Tangent & Trigonometric Ratios of Lines
questions.q: In the $xy$-plane, line $y = -\dfrac{3}{4}x + 6$ forms a right triangle with the positive coordinate axes. What is the value of $\sin\theta$, where $\theta$ is the acute angle the line makes with the $x$-axis?
questions.answer: The intercepts are $(8, 0)$ and $(0, 6)$, and the hypotenuse has length $\sqrt{8^2 + 6^2} = 10$. The side opposite the angle with the $x$-axis is $6$, so $\sin\theta = \dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, sides $a, b, c$ have lengths $13, 14, 15$. What is the length of the altitude to the side of length $14$?
questions.answer: Decompose the base $14$ into $5 + 9$: both $5\mathrm{-}12\mathrm{-}13$ and $9\mathrm{-}12\mathrm{-}15$ share the common altitude $h = 12$ (or by Heron's formula, $s = 21$, Area $= \sqrt{21(8)(7)(6)} = 84 = \dfrac{1}{2}(14)h \Rightarrow h = 12$).

questions.q: If $\sin\theta + \cos\theta = \dfrac{7}{5}$ for an acute angle $\theta$, what is the value of $\sin\theta\cos\theta$?
questions.answer: Square both sides: $(\sin\theta + \cos\theta)^2 = \sin^2\theta + \cos^2\theta + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = 1 + 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{49}{25} \Rightarrow 2\sin\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{24}{25} \Rightarrow \sin\theta\cos\theta = \dfrac{12}{25}$.

questions.target: Isoperimetric Area Ratio of Regular Polygons
questions.q: A regular hexagon and an equilateral triangle have the exact same perimeter. What is the ratio of the area of the regular hexagon to the area of the equilateral triangle?
questions.answer: Let the common perimeter be $6s$. The hexagon has side $s$ and consists of $6$ equilateral triangles of side $s$. The equilateral triangle has side $2s$ and area equal to $2^2 = 4$ equilateral triangles of side $s$. Thus the area ratio is $6 : 4 = 3 : 2$.

questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, angle bisectors of $\angle B$ and $\angle C$ intersect at the incenter $I$. If $\angle A = 68^{\circ}$, what is the measure of $\angle BIC$?
questions.answer: Since $\angle B + \angle C = 180^{\circ} - 68^{\circ} = 112^{\circ}$, half their sum is $\dfrac{1}{2}(\angle B + \angle C) = 56^{\circ}$. In $\triangle BIC$, $\angle BIC = 180^{\circ} - 56^{\circ} = 124^{\circ}$ (in general, $90^{\circ} + \dfrac{1}{2}\angle A$).

questions.q: Two poles of heights $10\,\mathrm{m}$ and $15\,\mathrm{m}$ stand vertically on level ground $20\,\mathrm{m}$ apart. A taut wire connects the top of each pole to the base of the opposite pole. At what height above the ground do the two wires intersect?
questions.answer: By the crossed-ladders harmonic property (independent of the horizontal separation $20\,\mathrm{m}$), the intersection height $h$ satisfies $\dfrac{1}{h} = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{1}{15} = \dfrac{5}{30} = \dfrac{1}{6} \Rightarrow h = 6\,\mathrm{m}$.

questions.target: Coordinate Triangle Area via Bounding Box / Shoelace
questions.q: What is the area of the triangle with vertices $(0, 0)$, $(6, 2)$, and $(3, 8)$ in the $xy$-plane?
questions.answer: By the shoelace formula (or bounding box $6 \times 8 = 48$ minus three right triangles of areas $6, 12, 9$), Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}|6(8) - 2(3)| = \dfrac{1}{2}(48 - 6) = 21$.
